About Zuiganji Temple and the Garyobai Plum Trees
Zuiganji Temple is located in Matsushima, Miyagi District, Miyagi Prefecture.
Two plum trees are planted in front of the main hall: a red-blossomed plum tree on the right and a white-blossomed one on the left. Their branches spread and twist along the ground, resembling a dragon lying down. This distinctive appearance is what gave the trees their name, "Garyobai" (Sleeping Dragon Plum).
According to legend, Date Masamune brought these trees back from Korea and planted them himself.
About Botanical Dyeing
Botanical dyeing is an innovative Japanese dyeing technique developed from traditional Japanese plant dyeing methods. As the name suggests, botanical dyeing uses natural materials such as plants, flowers, and berries to create dyes for coloring fabrics including cotton and wool.
Conventional plant dyeing typically uses approximately 20% natural dyes, while relying on a considerable amount of chemical agents to fix the color.
